name: Hemalite-GX
description: Hemalite-GX is a cast iron-cobalt alloy developed by Crucible Industries in partnership with BioForge, distinguished by a proprietary internal microvasculature network — laser-sintered channels 80-200 microns in diameter running throughout the bulk material — that is seeded with an engineered hemoglobin-analog fluid and a population of synthetic erythrocyte-like repair cells. The fluid carries oxygen and chemical repair precursors to damage sites, enabling crack-healing and corrosion remediation from within the metal itself. The system operates entirely on dissolved chemical gradients rather than requiring bioelectric input, making it the most autonomously self-sustaining bio-metal currently available.
cost: Φ2,100 per kg (industrial grade); Φ5,400 per kg (implant-compatible grade)
story_hooks: A century-old Hemalite-GX structural beam in a Shelf district building is still actively self-healing — the original hemoglobin-analog fluid has been replicating and mutating for a hundred years and now has properties that no one at Crucible Industries can fully account for.

Street-level augment hackers have discovered that Hemalite-GX's internal fluid network can be tapped and chemically reprogrammed to carry custom payloads — turning structural implant components into slow-release drug delivery systems without the host's knowledge.

A Crucible Industries whistleblower claims the hemoglobin-analog fluid in industrial-grade Hemalite-GX batches contains a classified chemical compound that accumulates in surrounding tissue over years of proximity — and the corporation has known about it since 2187.
